newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Commercial TV hits Slovakia with Markiza launch.
newsitem.headline: Commercial TV hits Slovakia with Markiza launch.

text.p: Commercial television comes to Slovakia for the first time on Saturday with the launch of TV Markiza.
The station's operators, Slovenska Televizna Spolocnost (STS), say it will have the potential to reach 60 percent of the population of five million.
STS is a joint venture between the local Markiza Slovakia s.r.o., which holds 51 percent, and Central European Media Enterprises (CME).

CME, a venture co-founded by New York cosmetics heir Ronald Lauder, is looking to build on its success in the neighbouring Czech Republic as a popular alternative to the grey face of state television in the former Eastern Bloc.

"Our rich experience with local partners in this region has convinced us that TV Markiza will fulfil all expectations and will become the most successful TV channel in Slovakia," CME executive chairman Leonard Fertig told a news conference on Friday.
Bermuda-based CME provided the entire start-up cost of Markiza of one billion Slovak crowns ($33 million), while the main contribution of the Slovak partners was the licence.

CME holds major stakes in four commercial TV stations in central and eastern Europe, including the first and most successful nationwide commercial television in the post-communist world -- TV Nova in the Czech Republic.
Fertig said CME would continue to expand its activities in the central and eastern Europe in the near future.
He said CME had amassed a cash pile of $200 million over the last few years which would be mainly invested in television projects in Ukraine, Poland and Hungary.

Within the next two years about 80 percent of the Slovak population should be able to receive Markiza's signal after the expansion of its network of transmitters to the more remote regions of hilly Slovakia.
The entry of Markiza onto the Slovak television market signals an end to the almost total monopoly of Slovak Television (STV), which is heavily monitored by the state.

Markiza aims to capture Slovakia's viewers with an agressive month-long advertising campaign in all media, boasting of plans to air spicy serials and action films. In the Czech Republic, TV Nova built a 70 percent market share in the first year after its launch in February 1994.
